html:
Two battles in October 42 BCE near Philippi in Macedonia, where Mark Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius, the leaders of Caesar's murderers.

Brutus and Cassius had gathered a large army in the east and held a strong position on the Via Egnatia. In the first battle Antony stormed Cassius's camp, while Brutus's men took Octavian's. Cassius, wrongly thinking all was lost, had himself killed. Three weeks later Brutus gave battle again and lost, and he too killed himself.

Antony won both fights; Octavian was ill and did little. With the "Liberators" gone, the cause of the old Republic died. The Second Triumvirate now split the Roman world between its members.

Veterans were settled at Philippi as a Roman colony. About ninety years later Paul the Apostle founded the first church in Europe there. Shakespeare's play Julius Caesar ends on this battlefield.
sum: Two battles in October 42 BCE near Philippi in Macedonia, where Mark Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius, the leaders of Caesar's murderers.
